_meta.model: gemini-3.1-flash-tts (also valid for other Gemini TTS models)

usage_notes.performance_instructions: Prepend natural-language directions to the text, like directing a voice actor. Controls style, accent, pace, tone, emotion. Example: "Say in a spooky whisper: '...'" or "soft, almost a whisper" / "anxious, rushed". Works per request; per-sentence direction = one short request per sentence (Vivarium narration pipeline does this).
usage_notes.inline_audio_tags: Inline modifiers inside the transcript give granular delivery control: [whispers], [laughs], [sighs], [excited], [bored], [shouting]. Example: "[whispers] Hey there... [shouting] and I can say things in many different ways."
usage_notes.multi_speaker: multiSpeakerVoiceConfig assigns up to 2 speakers each a prebuilt voice; the prompt can direct each separately, e.g. "Make Speaker1 sound tired and bored, and Speaker2 sound excited and happy".
usage_notes.director_notes_pattern: Best results structure: audio profile -> scene description -> director's notes (style/pacing/accent) -> transcript. Align all three levers: style prompt, emotionally-matching text, and markup tags should agree.
usage_notes.output_format: Returns base64 audio/l16;rate=24000 mono PCM in candidates[0].content.parts[0].inlineData — transcode server-side (ffmpeg) to Opus/MP3.
usage_notes.metering: usageMetadata.candidatesTokenCount (modality AUDIO) ~= 32 tokens per second of audio; billed at output-token rate.

vivarium_casting._note: all three are voice-profile-backed (per-language LAIONBox references): Leda="Lily", Puck="Peter", Iapetus="Ian"

narrator_experiment_2026-07-02.method: gemini-3.5-flash judged 0-10 on 'calm audiobook narrator, no acting, no vocal bursts' across 45+ generated samples (scripts/tts_narrator_experiment.py); full results in scripts/tts_experiment_summary.md
narrator_experiment_2026-07-02.prompt_finding: the prior default narration style scored a reliable 2/10 (3/3 draws) — reliably exhibited acted/performed delivery. A 'documentary narrator' framing scored 10/10/10 initially and held up best under repeated sampling.
narrator_experiment_2026-07-02.voice_finding: pooling all draws at temp=1.0 with the winning prompt: Iapetus 87.5% hit-rate (7/8 >=7, avg 9.0) vs. the old default Algenib 0% (0/3). Zubenelgenubi was second-best at 62.5%.
narrator_experiment_2026-07-02.temperature_finding: lowering TTS temperature below the default 1.0 did NOT improve reliability in this test (Iapetus: 67% @0.3, 50% @0.6, vs 87.5% @1.0) — kept at default.
narrator_experiment_2026-07-02.caveat: even the winning combo (Iapetus + documentary-narrator prompt) is not 100% reliable — roughly 1-in-8 draws still shows an audible vocal burst or performed delivery. This appears to be inherent TTS model randomness, not fixable by prompt/voice/temperature choice alone.
